newsitem.title: USA: CBOT says supports findings on March wheat expiry.
newsitem.headline: CBOT says supports findings on March wheat expiry.

text.p: A CBOT spokeswoman said the exchange stood by its conduct committee's findings on penalties for a March wheat trading frenzy that sent prices to a record $7.50 per bushel.

"We do stand by what the conduct committee found," the spokeswoman said. "They made their decision based on the information available at that time and the CFTC was kept abreast of all of the actions of this conduct committee."

Six participants in the trading were given letters of reprimand from the CBOT conduct committee. Louis Dreyfus Corp and subsidiary Term Commodities jointly paid $10,000 because they wrongly sold wheat in a modified closing call held a few minutes after the expiry.
U.S. regulators, acting on a staff report that alleged inadequate penalties for trading after the expiry of the March wheat contract, said Friday they would review the CBOT's disciplinary actions.
The staff report suggested the CFTC should direct the exchange to impose more stringent penalties but gave the CBOT and participants in the trading 30 days to respond.
